subject: SRW
body:
The collection of rare stamps, which includes several items from the 1800s, ______ on display at the city museum.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular 'collection', not 'stamps' or 'items'.

subject: SRW
body:
Each of the researchers ______ required to submit a summary of findings by Friday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Each' is singular.

subject: SRW
body:
The results of the long-term study ______ that regular sleep improves memory.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the plural 'results'.

subject: SRW
body:
Neither the coach nor the players ______ expecting the storm to delay the match.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'players'.

subject: SRW
body:
The team of engineers ______ finalising its design for the new bridge.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Team' is a singular collective noun here, and 'its' confirms this.

subject: SRW
body:
Along the river ______ several old mills that once powered the town.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: In this inverted sentence the subject is the plural 'mills'.

subject: SRW
body:
The number of students applying to study engineering ______ risen sharply.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'The number' is singular.

subject: SRW
body:
A number of volunteers ______ offered to help clean the beach.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'A number of' means 'several' and takes a plural verb.

subject: SRW
body:
The data from both satellites, collected over a decade, ______ a clear warming trend.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Here 'data' is treated as plural, matching the formal style of the sentence.

subject: SRW
body:
Mathematics, along with chemistry and physics, ______ a required subject for this programme.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Phrases like 'along with' don't change the singular subject 'Mathematics'.

subject: SRW
body:
The flock of migrating geese ______ south every autumn.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Flock' is singular.

subject: SRW
body:
The instructions on the back of the box ______ easy to follow.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the plural 'instructions'.

subject: SRW
body:
Either the manager or her assistants ______ the reports each week.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With 'either…or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'assistants'.

subject: SRW
body:
Every one of the paintings in the gallery ______ been restored.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Every one' is singular.

subject: SRW
body:
The committee, after weeks of debate, ______ its final decision.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Committee' acting as one body is singular, matching 'its'.

subject: SRW
body:
Among the most famous works in the collection ______ a portrait painted in 1651.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: In this inverted sentence the subject is the singular 'portrait'.

subject: SRW
body:
The volcano had been dormant for centuries ______ scientists were surprised by the sudden eruption.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Two independent clauses joined by 'therefore' need a semicolon before it and a comma after.

subject: SRW
body:
Marie Curie won two Nobel Prizes ______ one in physics and one in chemistry.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A colon introduces an explanation or list that follows a complete clause.

subject: SRW
body:
The bakery opens at 6 a.m. ______ most customers arrive after 8 a.m.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A comma goes before the coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses.

subject: SRW
body:
Although the experiment failed twice ______ the team refused to give up.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Put a comma after an introductory dependent clause.

subject: SRW
body:
The novelist ______ latest book was translated into twelve languages, will speak at the festival.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A non-essential clause is set off by commas; 'whose' shows possession.

subject: SRW
body:
The company announced that ______ new headquarters will open next spring.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Its' is possessive; 'it's' means 'it is'.

subject: SRW
body:
The students handed in ______ projects before the deadline.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Their' is the plural possessive.

subject: SRW
body:
Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor ______ they support about a quarter of all marine species.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Use a comma before 'yet' when it joins two independent clauses.

subject: SRW
body:
The museum's newest exhibit features three ______ a dinosaur skeleton, a meteorite and an ancient map.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A colon after a complete clause introduces the list.

subject: SRW
body:
Lagos, ______ one of Africa's largest cities, is a major centre for music and film.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A city–country pair takes a comma after the country when the sentence continues.

subject: SRW
body:
The ______ findings were published in a leading journal.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Plural possessive of 'scientists' adds only an apostrophe.

subject: SRW
body:
The chef tasted the ______ then added a pinch of salt.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A compound verb (tasted … added) needs no comma.

subject: SRW
body:
The festival attracts thousands of ______ many travel from neighbouring countries to attend.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon.

subject: SRW
body:
Dr Okafor's research focuses on one ______ how plants respond to drought.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A colon introduces the explanation of 'one question'.

subject: SRW
body:
Kenya's runners, ______ have won many Olympic medals, often train at high altitude.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Who' is the subject of the clause and refers to people.

subject: SRW
body:
The city's two ______ the old harbour and the new marina, attract many tourists.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The appositive naming the ports is set off by a pair of commas.

subject: SRW
body:
After the storm ______ volunteers gathered to clear fallen trees from the roads.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A comma follows the introductory clause.

subject: SRW
body:
The guide ______ was written by a local historian, explains the town's history in detail.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A non-essential clause beginning with 'which' is set off by commas.

subject: SRW
body:
Several ______ including copper, cobalt and lithium, are needed to make modern batteries.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Including…' is a non-essential phrase set off by commas.

subject: SRW
body:
The ______ new uniforms arrived just before the season began.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Singular possessive: team's.

subject: SRW
body:
By the time the rescue team arrived, the hikers ______ for over six hours.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The past perfect continuous shows an action continuing up to a past moment.

subject: SRW
body:
Next year, the city ______ a new rail line linking the airport to downtown.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Next year' calls for the future tense.

subject: SRW
body:
In 1969, astronauts ______ on the Moon for the first time.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A completed event at a specific past time uses the simple past.

subject: SRW
body:
Since 2015, the charity ______ more than 200 schools.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: 'Since' + a time up to now takes the present perfect.

subject: SRW
body:
The artist, who grew up in Accra, ______ her first exhibition in 2010.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A finished action in a stated past year uses the simple past.

subject: SRW
body:
Every morning, the farmer ______ the cows before sunrise.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A habitual present action uses the simple present.

subject: SRW
body:
Many people assume bats are blind. ______ most bats can see quite well, and some species see in colour.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence corrects a misconception, so 'In fact' fits.

subject: SRW
body:
Solar panels have become much cheaper over the past decade. ______ more households are installing them.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence is a consequence of the first.

subject: SRW
body:
The first draft of the report was clear and well organised. ______ it contained several factual errors.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence contrasts with the praise in the first.

subject: SRW
body:
Octopuses can solve puzzles to reach food. ______ some have learned to unscrew jar lids.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence gives a specific example of puzzle-solving.

subject: SRW
body:
The museum extended its opening hours. ______ it reduced ticket prices for students.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence adds another, similar action.

subject: SRW
body:
Most desert plants store water in thick stems. ______ some rely instead on very deep roots.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence presents a different strategy.

subject: SRW
body:
The bridge was built to last 50 years. ______ it is still in use after more than a century.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence reports something surprising given the first.

subject: SRW
body:
The team tested the vaccine in mice. ______ they moved on to small human trials.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The sentences describe steps in time order.

subject: SRW
body:
Bees pollinate many fruit crops. ______ a decline in bee populations could reduce harvests.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence draws a logical conclusion.

subject: SRW
body:
The novel received poor reviews when it was first published. ______ it is now considered a classic.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence contrasts past and present reception.

subject: SRW
body:
Chess requires careful planning several moves ahead. ______ go, a strategy game from East Asia, rewards long-term thinking.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: Both sentences make the same kind of point about different games.

subject: SRW
body:
The city planned to build a new stadium. ______ residents voted to spend the money on schools.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence describes what happened in place of the plan.

subject: SRW
body:
Some critics praised the film's bold visual style. ______ others felt the story was too slow.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The sentence introduces a different, contrasting view.

subject: SRW
body:
The recipe calls for fresh tomatoes. ______ canned tomatoes can be used if fresh ones are unavailable.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence qualifies the first.

subject: SRW
body:
The athlete trained for six hours a day for a year. ______ she won the national championship.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The second sentence gives the final outcome.

subject: SRW
body:
Plastic waste harms marine life. ______ turtles often mistake plastic bags for jellyfish.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: A specific example follows a general claim.

subject: SRW
body:
The company's profits fell last year. ______ it hired 200 new employees.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: Hiring despite falling profits is unexpected.

subject: SRW
body:
First, the clay is shaped on a wheel. ______ it is dried and fired in a kiln.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: The sentences describe a sequence.

subject: SRW
body:
The study was small, involving only 30 participants. ______ its findings should be confirmed by larger studies.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: A conclusion follows from the study's small size.

subject: SRW
body:
Many early cars were steam-powered. ______ most cars today run on petrol, diesel or electricity.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: Past and present technologies are contrasted.

subject: SRW
body:
The scientist's explanation was so ______ that even students with no background in physics could follow it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Lucid' means clear and easy to understand.

subject: SRW
body:
Although the senator was usually talkative, she remained ______ when reporters asked about her plans.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Reticent' means unwilling to say much; the contrast with 'talkative' signals this.

subject: SRW
body:
The new policy was meant to be temporary, but it proved so popular that it became ______.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: The contrast with 'temporary' points to 'permanent'.

subject: SRW
body:
The historian warned that the diary, written decades after the events, might not be an entirely ______ source.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Writing long after events could make a source less reliable.

subject: SRW
body:
Rather than accepting the first answer, the detective was ______, questioning every witness twice.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Meticulous' means very careful and precise.

subject: SRW
body:
The plant is ______ to the region: it grows naturally there and nowhere else.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Endemic' means native to and restricted to a place.

subject: SRW
body:
Supplies were so ______ during the drought that families were limited to a few litres of water a day.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Limits on water suggest supplies were scarce.

subject: SRW
body:
The architect's design was ______: it combined traditional Hausa patterns with modern glass and steel.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Combining old and new in a new way is innovative.

subject: SRW
body:
Early results were promising, but the researchers remained ______, noting that the sample size was small.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Noting a limitation shows caution.

subject: SRW
body:
The author's argument is ______ by strong evidence from three independent studies.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Strong evidence supports an argument.

subject: SRW
body:
The mayor's speech was ______, lasting only two minutes but covering every key point.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: 'Concise' means brief but complete.

subject: SRW
body:
Because the bridge was ______, engineers closed it until repairs could be made.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Closing a bridge for repairs implies it was unsafe.

subject: SRW
body:
The two theories are ______: if one is true, the other must be false.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Theories that can't both be true are incompatible.

subject: SRW
body:
In the poem, the storm is ______ for the speaker's inner turmoil.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: The storm stands for the speaker's feelings.

subject: SRW
body:
The documentary offers a ______ portrait of the musician, showing both her talents and her flaws.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Showing strengths and flaws is balanced.

subject: SRW
body:
The old manuscript was so ______ that researchers handled it only with gloves.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Handling it carefully suggests it was easily damaged.

subject: SRW
body:
Her ______ to the project was clear: she worked evenings and weekends to finish it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Working extra hours shows commitment.

subject: SRW
body:
The evidence was ______; it could be interpreted in several different ways.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Evidence open to several readings is ambiguous.

subject: SRW
body:
Unlike his ______ brother, who spent freely, Tomas saved most of his earnings.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: The contrast with saving points to spending freely.

subject: SRW
body:
The report ______ the main causes of the flood, listing them in order of importance.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Listing causes identifies them.

subject: SRW
body:
Scientists were ______ by the results, which contradicted decades of earlier research.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Unexpected results surprise people.

subject: SRW
body:
The negotiators reached a ______ that satisfied both sides.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: An agreement satisfying both sides is a compromise.

subject: SRW
body:
The lecture was ______, drawing on examples from history, biology and music.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: Many fields of examples shows breadth.

subject: SRW
body:
The village's population has ______ steadily as young people move to the cities.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
explanation: People leaving makes the population shrink.

subject: SRW
body:
Researchers studying sleep found that students who slept at least eight hours before an exam scored, on average, 10% higher than those who slept five hours or less. The researchers caution that students who sleep more may also differ in other ways, such as how much they studied.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: More sleep is linked to higher scores, though other factors may explain the link.
Studying is less important than sleep for exam success.
Sleeping more than eight hours guarantees a higher exam score.
Students who study more always sleep less.
explanation: The text reports a link but warns it may not be causal.

subject: SRW
body:
The baobab tree can store thousands of litres of water in its thick trunk. During long dry seasons, when little rain falls, the tree draws on this store to survive. Its leafless branches in the dry season also reduce water loss.

According to the text, how does the baobab survive dry seasons?
options: By absorbing moisture from the air through its leaves
By growing deep roots to reach groundwater
By storing water in its trunk and reducing water loss
By producing seeds that wait for rain
explanation: The text mentions trunk storage and leafless branches.

subject: SRW
body:
In 1957, Ghana became the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule. Its first leader, Kwame Nkrumah, argued that independence for one nation was incomplete without the liberation of the whole continent.

Based on the text, Nkrumah most likely believed that
options: Ghana should remain under colonial rule.
African nations should support one another's independence.
Economic growth was more important than independence.
explanation: He saw Ghana's independence as linked to the continent's.

subject: SRW
body:
Some urban planners argue that adding more lanes to highways reduces traffic. Others point to a pattern called 'induced demand': as roads widen, more people choose to drive, and congestion soon returns.

The second sentence mainly serves to
options: summarise the history of highway building
give an example that supports the first sentence
define a term used in the first sentence
present a view that challenges the claim in the first sentence
explanation: 'Induced demand' is offered as a counter-argument.

subject: SRW
body:
Text 1: Many economists believe a four-day work week will lower productivity, since employees will simply have less time to work.
Text 2: Trials in several companies found that output stayed the same or rose, because rested employees worked more efficiently.

How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1?
options: By agreeing that productivity always falls
By saying that trials are not useful evidence
By claiming that employees prefer longer weeks
By arguing that efficiency gains can offset fewer hours
explanation: Text 2's evidence directly answers Text 1's concern.

subject: SRW
body:
A biologist hypothesised that a species of frog changes colour to match its surroundings. She placed frogs on light and dark backgrounds and recorded their colour after one hour.

Which finding would most directly support her hypothesis?
options: The frogs' colour did not change.
Frogs ate more on dark backgrounds.
Frogs on dark backgrounds became darker, and frogs on light backgrounds became lighter.
All frogs became darker regardless of background.
explanation: This result matches colour changing to match surroundings.

subject: SRW
body:
The author describes the old market as 'a maze of colour and noise, where traders called out prices over the clatter of carts and the smell of spices hung in the air.'

The sentence mainly serves to
options: argue that the market should be closed
compare the market with a supermarket
create a vivid sensory picture of the market
explanation: It appeals to sight, sound and smell.

subject: SRW
body:
A recent survey of 2,000 adults found that 65% read at least one book in the past year, down from 74% a decade earlier. However, the share listening to audiobooks rose from 12% to 30%.

Which conclusion is best supported by the survey?
options: Audiobooks caused the decline in reading.
Reading printed books has declined while audiobook listening has grown.
explanation: The figures show the two trends without proving cause.

subject: SRW
body:
Honeybees communicate the location of food through a 'waggle dance.' The angle of the dance relative to vertical shows the direction of the food compared with the sun, and the length of the waggle shows the distance.

According to the text, what does the length of the waggle indicate?
options: How far away the food is
explanation: The text links waggle length to distance.

subject: SRW
body:
The engineer's notes say: 'Prototype A was lighter but cracked under heavy loads. Prototype B was heavier but showed no damage after 10,000 test cycles.'

Which choice best uses the notes to explain why the team chose Prototype B?
options: Prototype A was chosen because it never cracked.
Prototype B was chosen because it was lighter.
Prototype B was chosen because, though heavier, it proved more durable in testing.
explanation: The notes show B's durability outweighed its extra weight.

subject: SRW
body:
The Ethiopian calendar has thirteen months: twelve months of thirty days each and a short thirteenth month of five or six days. As a result, its dates differ from the Gregorian calendar used in most countries.

Which choice best describes the function of the second sentence?
options: It gives an example of a month.
It states a consequence of the calendar's structure.
It explains the history of the calendar.
explanation: 'As a result' signals a consequence.

subject: SRW
body:
Mangrove forests protect coastlines by absorbing the energy of waves. After a major storm, villages behind healthy mangroves reported far less damage than villages where mangroves had been cleared.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Villagers should clear mangroves after storms.
Mangroves help reduce storm damage to coastal communities.
explanation: The example supports the protective role of mangroves.

subject: SRW
body:
In a study, one group of plants was played music for two hours a day, and another group was kept in silence. After a month, the two groups were the same height.

Which conclusion is best supported by the study?
options: The music had no measurable effect on plant height in this study.
explanation: Equal heights show no effect on height.

subject: SRW
body:
The writer begins by describing a crowded bus at dawn, then introduces the driver, Mr Adeyemi, who has driven the same route for thirty years.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It presents a problem and offers a solution.
It argues for a change in transport policy.
It sets a scene and then focuses on a particular person.
explanation: Scene first, then a character.

subject: SRW
body:
Text 1: Some historians argue that the printing press spread new ideas quickly across Europe.
Text 2: Others note that most people could not read in the 1500s, so printed books reached only a small, educated group at first.

Based on the texts, the author of Text 2 would most likely say that Text 1
options: overstates how quickly ideas reached most people
is completely wrong about the printing press
agrees with Text 2 in every way
explanation: Text 2 qualifies how widely ideas spread.

subject: SRW
body:
A student claims that people who exercise regularly sleep better. To support this claim, she cites a survey in which 70% of regular exercisers reported good sleep, compared with 45% of people who rarely exercised.

Which choice best describes how the survey relates to the student's claim?
options: It shows an association that supports the claim.
It is unrelated to the claim.
It proves that exercise causes better sleep.
explanation: A survey can show a link but not prove cause.

subject: SRW
body:
While researching a topic, a student took these notes:
• The Great Green Wall is an African-led project to restore land across the Sahel.
• It aims to restore 100 million hectares of degraded land by 2030.
• It spans countries from Senegal to Djibouti.

The student wants to emphasise the project's scale. Which choice best does this?
options: Stretching from Senegal to Djibouti, the Great Green Wall aims to restore 100 million hectares of land by 2030.
Many projects aim to restore land.
The Sahel is a region in Africa.
The Great Green Wall is an African-led project.
explanation: It combines the distance and the area target.

subject: SRW
body:
A student took these notes:
• Ada Lovelace worked with Charles Babbage on the Analytical Engine.
• In 1843 she published notes describing an algorithm for the machine.
• She is often called the first computer programmer.

The student wants to explain why Lovelace is called the first programmer. Which choice best does this?
options: Ada Lovelace worked with Charles Babbage.
The Analytical Engine was a machine.
Because she published an algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine in 1843, Lovelace is often called the first programmer.
explanation: It links the algorithm to the title.

subject: SRW
body:
A student took these notes:
• Lake Victoria is Africa's largest lake by area.
• It is shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania.
• It is a source of the White Nile.

The student wants to introduce Lake Victoria to readers unfamiliar with it. Which choice best does this?
options: Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake, is shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania and feeds the White Nile.
Lake Victoria is larger than some other lakes.
The White Nile has several sources.
explanation: It gives the key identifying facts.

subject: SRW
body:
A student took these notes:
• Study A: students who took handwritten notes remembered more concepts.
• Study B: students who typed notes wrote down more words.

The student wants to contrast the two studies' findings. Which choice best does this?
options: Students take notes in different ways.
While typing let students record more words, handwriting helped them remember more concepts.
explanation: 'While' sets up the contrast between the findings.

subject: SRW
body:
A student took these notes:
• Teff is a tiny grain native to Ethiopia.
• It is used to make injera, a spongy flatbread.
• Teff is naturally gluten-free.

The student wants to highlight a health-related feature of teff. Which choice best does this?
options: Teff, the grain used to make injera, is naturally gluten-free.
explanation: Gluten-free is the health-related feature.

subject: SRW
body:
A student took these notes:
• Wangari Maathai founded the Green Belt Movement in Kenya in 1977.
• The movement planted over 50 million trees.
• In 2004 she became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

The student wants to emphasise Maathai's achievement as a Nobel laureate. Which choice best does this?
options: In 2004, Wangari Maathai became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.
The movement planted many trees in Kenya.
The Green Belt Movement was founded in 1977.
explanation: It focuses on the Nobel Prize.
